source.title: TabSTAR: A Tabular Foundation Model for Tabular Data with Text Fields
source.authors: Alan Arazi; Eilam Shapira; Roi Reichart

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance as pretraining data scale changes in a tabular foundation model, a setting distinct from language-model parameter, token, or compute scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream AUROC and R2 by number of TabSTAR pretraining datasets. It does not report held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws, or test extrapolation. References to language-model scaling laws are contextual, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures downstream classification and regression performance as TabSTAR pretraining increases from 0 to 16, 64 and 256 tabular datasets. These results bear on V6 in a new setting, although they do not establish a predictive scaling equation or a power-law form.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report increasing average downstream performance with more pretraining datasets and propose further data and model scaling. Although the abstract calls this scaling laws, the study supplies no power-law fit or extrapolation test, and task-level results are not uniformly monotonic.
record.recipe_differences: Measures TabSTAR downstream AUROC/R2 across the number of pretraining tabular datasets, rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy across parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with pretraining dataset count and task type; dataset-level changes are not uniformly monotonic. The scaling analysis evaluates 20 downstream datasets.
record.problems: The scaling analysis uses four pretraining-data counts and downstream metrics, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy; it reports no power-law fit, exponent, or extrapolation test. The analysis is limited to 20 downstream datasets, and some dataset-level scores do not improve monotonically.
record.rows_left_out: Table 30 reports 80 dataset-by-pretraining-count scores. To stay within 60 rows, the record includes the 20 zero-pretraining reference scores, the 20 scores at 256 datasets, and selected intermediate scores showing declines or flat results, alongside all eight aggregate Table 29 results. Other intermediate dataset-level scores from Table 30 are omitted.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling over parameters, tokens or compute across orders of magnitude.
Small-run power-law fits predicting substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/data allocation and its exponents.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count; Appendix A.3 changes parameter counts or mechanisms without establishing this controlled comparison.
Whether a power-law form holds beyond text pretraining; improving tabular downstream scores alone does not establish that form.
A quantitatively validated predictive relationship, extrapolation beyond tested dataset counts, model-size scaling, and downstream performance predicted from pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices, and departures from a fitted single power law.

record.verdict_notes: The positive-count variants use nested pretraining subsets. With up to 2,048 examples sampled per dataset per epoch, increasing dataset count also increases training exposure; this is not a fixed-compute experiment. The zero-pretraining comparison additionally changes downstream adaptation from full finetuning to LoRA. Confidence intervals describe individual scores, not paired differences, so overlap alone does not establish absence or significance. Intermediate Table 30 omissions are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation between model parameters and training tokens.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
TabSTAR is a tabular model, but the study does not establish that the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
Tests downstream scores against number of pretraining datasets for TabSTAR; does not test downstream performance against language-model scale or pretraining loss.
No analysis of scaling-law exponent or compute-optimal-fit dependence on setup, or of curves bending away from a power law.

relationships.condition: Average downstream performance over eight classification and twelve regression datasets
relationships.reason: R1–R8 show increasing normalized averages at every tested pretraining count: classification 0.352 to 0.786 and regression 0.338 to 0.811.
relationships.display_finding: Normalized averages increased at every tested pretraining dataset total, from 0.352 to 0.786 for classification and 0.338 to 0.811 for regression.

relationships.condition: Larger endpoint gains on C07, R03, R05, R18, R30 and R34
relationships.reason: R33, R38, R39, R43, R46 and R48 report higher downstream scores at 256 datasets than at zero pretraining; these support an improvement trend without establishing a predictive formula.
relationships.display_finding: Selected datasets achieved higher downstream scores after pretraining on 256 datasets than without pretraining, without establishing a predictive formula.

relationships.condition: Tasks with small endpoint gains or nonmonotonic intermediate point estimates
relationships.reason: R29–R32, R34, R36–R37, R40–R42, R44–R45, R47 and R49–R59 show that average improvement does not imply uniform task-level improvement; individual declines are not established as significant.
relationships.display_finding: Individual tasks showed small endpoint gains or nonmonotonic intermediate estimates, although the observed declines were not established as statistically significant.

relationships.condition: C12 endpoint comparison, zero versus 256 pretraining datasets
relationships.reason: R35 reports identical AUROC of 98.3 at both endpoints, showing no downstream improvement at the reported precision for this task.
relationships.display_finding: AUROC was 98.3 at both endpoints, showing no improvement at the reported precision.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate classification and regression results across 16, 64, and 256 pretraining datasets
reader_labels.reason: Both reported downstream aggregates rise with more pretraining datasets; see R2-R4 and R6-R8.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Dataset-level results in the analysis set
reader_labels.reason: Several intermediate or endpoint results are flat, small, or below the 0-dataset reference, so the aggregate trend is not uniform per dataset; see R29-R30, R32, R34-R36, R49-R59.
